newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU agrees new third country lending system.
newsitem.headline: EU agrees new third country lending system.

text.p: The European Union on Monday agreed a new system for lending money to third countries, raising the amount available by lowering the sum that must be guaranteed.
After months of disagreement on the issue, finance ministers from the 15-nation bloc reached a political deal that will allow the European Investment Bank (EIB) to boost its loans.
As part of the deal, they also agreed to set up a "substantial" facility to lend money to central and eastern European countries lining up to join the EU.
Some of the details of this so-called "pre-accession support facility" will be put off for a while until the actual countries likely to be eligible are agreed, possibly next year.
The main change in the overall EIB lending system will be to set a guarantee level of 70 percent, compared with the current 100 percent.
The move means the EIB will be able to lend more money than is guaranteed by the 15 EU member states.
